_comment: SaaS tenant registry - copy to tenants.json (git-ignored, chmod 600) and set TENANTS_FILE. Without a registry file the agent serves the single built-in 'default' tenant from .env, exactly the classic behaviour. NEVER bake this file into the image (.dockerignore excludes it): it holds every organization's secrets, and the compose files mount it read-only at runtime. After editing: POST /infra/reload-tenants with X-Agent-Token - no rebuild, no restart, no downtime for orgs already being served.
_org_key_rules: Lowercase, URL-safe, stable forever - it appears in every web-chat URL (/webhooks/<org>/webchat/...) and prefixes that org's chat memory and Qdrant collections. Renaming one orphans both. Never use 'webchat' (it would collide with the non-org route) or 'default'.

_how_a_request_finds_its_org.whatsapp: the <org> segment of /webhooks/<org>/whatsapp/<channel_id>/ - which is also the only thing Meta's VERIFICATION GET carries, since it has no payload - and, on a message POST, the Phone Number ID matched against phone_number_ids
_how_a_request_finds_its_org.admin endpoints: the X-Agent-Token header, matched against api_token (the shared operator token authenticates but names no org, so it cannot reindex)
_how_a_request_finds_its_org._if_none_of_them_do: With STRICT_TENANCY=true the request is refused with 400. Without it, the request is served from the default tenant built from .env - which means an inquiry created in whichever company that points at, silently. Keep strict mode on whenever this file holds more than one organization.

sanabl._note: A group running its own CRM. backend_url points at THAT group's .NET API - the agent is shared, the CRM and its SQL Server are not.

alnoor._note: A second group. Nothing is shared with sanabl: different backend, different token, different Gemini quota, different Qdrant collections. One org's chat cannot reach another's data even if a bug tried to.

_field_notes.backend_url: REQUIRED. The org's own OnlineCampus .NET API. Wrong value = that org answers 500 while every other org is fine, so check per-org after onboarding, not just /health.
_field_notes.api_token: REQUIRED, and must be UNIQUE per org - it is also how an admin call identifies which organization is calling. Reusing one across orgs makes them indistinguishable.
_field_notes.google_api_key: Optional. Omit to fall back to the shared GOOGLE_API_KEY in .env. Set it to give the org its own quota and billing.
_field_notes.qdrant_prefix: Defaults to the org key. Collections are named <prefix>-<agent_id>, which is what keeps one school's documents out of another's answers.
_field_notes.phone_number_ids: Meta Phone Number IDs, as strings. This is the ONLY way a WhatsApp webhook is routed to an org - an ID missing here means that number's messages cannot be served. A group with several numbers lists them all.
_field_notes.webchat_origins: Browser origins allowed to call this org's webchat endpoints, exactly as the browser sends them (scheme + host + port, no path, no trailing slash). The agent builds its CORS allow-list from this registry on every request, so adding an origin takes effect at the next reload with no restart. Empty = that org's website cannot reach the chat - and CORS failure is invisible server-side: the request arrives, the agent answers, the browser discards the reply.
